quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You do not need to use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If there is no gap in traffic when entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If there is no gap in traffic, slow down on the ramp to wait for one. Do not stop at the end of the ramp because you will not have enough space to speed up to match traffic before entering.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to the curb and when leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal both when pulling next to a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a driver?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces safe driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot or be missed easily. Always stay alert and look for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using emergency lights or sirens. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without using sirens or flashing lights, you do not need to get out of the way. Drive normally.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop along the road at night?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams.
questions.explanation: If you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time when possible. If you need to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian safely.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.explanation: Stop signs are always octagonal (eight-sided). This shape tells drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrian waves first.
Only if the pedestrian is not using a phone.

questions.explanation: Always stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may proceed carefully only when the crosswalk is completely clear.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert and careful. Slow down as you approach it.

questions.question: How fast you drive does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you hit the brakes.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Always stay far behind other vehicles so you have enough room to stop.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to tell the cyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bike lane to pass them.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Cyclists have less protection than drivers. Slow down and give them as much space as possible. Passing too quickly can knock them off course.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Stay to the right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Being tired and being drunk affect your driving in similar ways. 18 hours without sleep impairs you like 0.05% alcohol. 24 hours without sleep impairs you like 0.10% alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead is one-way traffic only.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass or meet a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What should you always do when approaching a roundabout?
questions.explanation: Roundabouts are designed for low-speed driving. Always slow down as you approach one.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Either driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: If you and another vehicle arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. You must yield to them, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to all drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. Park only where traffic is not blocked and other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.

questions.question: If you drive slower than traffic around you, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You may drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you block normal traffic movement by driving too slowly, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots you cannot see. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road is closed to traffic.

questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about work zones and dangerous conditions ahead. Slow down and drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check traffic behind you often to spot tailgaters. If another car is too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance at night when it is hard to see. Use headlights correctly. Do not look at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: This sign shows a type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, drive at:

options.text: About the same speed as freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: About the same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at about the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is faster than the legal speed limit.
